title: ThermalScope: A Practical Interrupt Side Channel Attack Based on Thermal Event Interrupts
problem: Thermal event interrupts triggered at fixed CPU temperature thresholds can be exploited as a side channel to leak information about CPU workloads and system secrets. The attack observes that different workloads generate distinct heat signatures that correlate with thermal interrupt activation.
motivation: Demonstrating new side channel attacks through thermal interrupts reveals previously unexplored vulnerabilities in modern CPUs and operating systems that could compromise system confidentiality.
method: ThermalScope watches when thermal event interrupts fire—these are automatic alerts triggered at fixed CPU temperature thresholds set by the hardware manufacturer. Different computations produce different heat patterns, so the timing of these interrupts reveals what the CPU is doing. The attack uses two heat-amplifying techniques to make the heat signatures stronger and easier to detect, and it works both when code runs directly on the operating system and inside a web browser.
key_novelty: It's the first side-channel attack that leaks system secrets by observing thermal event interrupts (automatic temperature-triggered alerts at fixed CPU thresholds) that fire as the CPU heats up during computation.
contributions: Proposes ThermalScope, a new thermal event interrupt-based side channel attack applicable to both native and browser environments
Demonstrates correlation between thermal event interrupt activation and CPU temperature levels with practical validation on Intel CPUs
Implements heat amplifying techniques to reliably enhance thermal fingerprint signals for attack effectiveness
Demonstrates practical attacks: covert channel transmission (0.1 b/s), DNN model fingerprinting (90%+ accuracy), and KASLR breaking within 8.2 hours
